assessment.summary: EGFR (P00533) is one of the most well-validated and extensively drugged targets in oncology, with 393 PDB structures (best resolution 1.07Å), 26,600 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 20 approved drugs including small molecules and biologics. The target has outstanding structural, chemical, and literature support, making it a benchmark for high druggability. Ongoing research continues to address resistance mechanisms and novel indications such as glioblastoma.
evidence_gaps: Median IC50 of 2000 nM suggests a large fraction of screened compounds have modest potency, indicating selectivity and potency optimization remain non-trivial for new chemical series

AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 75.9 with only 70.7% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (e.g., extracellular domain, flexible loops) are not fully captured structurally, though kinase domain is well resolved by X-ray
Resistance mutations (e.g., T790M, C797S, exon 20 insertions) limit the utility of existing drugs and create ongoing druggability challenges for next-generation inhibitors
CNS penetrance of current approved drugs is limited, which is relevant for indications like glioblastoma highlighted in recent literature
Tissue-specific and mutation-specific efficacy profiles are not fully captured by aggregate ChEMBL or PDB data
